title: Incremental State Delta Transport Format — Notebook
content:
Purpose: capture a lightweight, incremental transport format for session state deltas so client-side proxies and edge adapters can stream small changes to the backend (and vice versa) without shipping full blobs on every update.

Context / motivation:
- Current session snapshot flow is: client -> full snapshot upload -> backend validate -> store. This is robust but expensive for chat apps where most updates are small (new messages, small KV edits).
- We want a compact on-wire format that:
  * expresses small edits to conversation state (append, patch, tombstone)
  * supports causal ordering and simple resume semantics
  * is friendly to partial-replay (able to rehydrate from a base snapshot + ordered delta stream)
  * works over unreliable connections and allows gap-repair

Constraints / non-goals:
- Not aiming to replace full snapshot storage formats (we still keep canonical epochal bundle). This is a transport optimization.
- Not a general CRDT spec — keep design intentionally pragmatic: small ops + sequence and acks.

High-level design:
1) Base snapshot concept: a full opaque blob identified by base_snapshot_id and base_seq (epoch).
2) Deltas are small ops with a type tag, target path, optional op payload, an incremental sequence number, and causal parent pointer (parent_seq or parent_digest).
3) Transport guarantees: at-least-once delivery (we expect duplicates) + monotonic local seqs. Server acks highest contiguous seq seen for a session; client reconciles gaps.

Minimal delta envelope (ASCII sketch):
{
  "session_id": "str",
  "base_snapshot_id": "str | null",
  "base_seq": "int | 0",
  "delta_seq": "int",            // strictly increasing per session/stream
  "parent_seq": "int | null",
  "op_type": "append|replace|delete|patch|kv_set|kv_del|meta_update",
  "target": "/conversation/messages[12]" | "/kv/user.prefs/theme",
  "payload": "base64-json" /* small JSON blob for op */,
  "hint_size": "int",       // uncompressed payload size for sizing decisions
  "client_ts": "rfc3339",
  "trace_id": "str"
}

Examples of ops:
- append message:
  op_type: append
  target: /conversation/messages
  payload: {"author":"user","text":"Hey, update","metadata":{"token_est":24}}

- kv set:
  op_type: kv_set
  target: /kv/anchors:recent_phrases
  payload: {"key":"grocery-list","value":"milk,eggs"}

- tombstone message:
  op_type: delete
  target: /conversation/messages[23]

Sequencing and reconciliation:
- Each delta_seq increments per client stream. parent_seq is used by server to detect reorders and simple forks. If server sees parent_seq != expected, it will mark delta as out-of-order and request re-sync.
- Server ACK frame: {session_id, acked_seq, received_digest, server_ts} -> client can garbage collect local journal up to acked_seq.
- Gap repair: client retains journal of sent deltas until acked. On reconnect, client sends resume request: {session_id, from_seq} and streams remaining deltas. Server may respond with a merge directive if conflict detected.

Merge / conflict model (pragmatic):
- If a delta targets the same index (e.g., replace vs append), server resolves using last-write-wins by delta_seq with server-assigned authority on final ordering, then emits a reconcile delta for clients subscribing to session changes.
- For KV keys, server can accept last-write-wins or apply simple numeric bump strategies (TBD per key).

Wire transport layers considered:
- HTTP/2 streaming / SSE: simple but may require reconnect logic.
- WebSocket with an ack/journal model: low latency and symmetric.
- gRPC bidi stream: strong TLS+loadbalancer story; worth prototyping.

API sketches (REST/http POST and WS frames):
- POST /session/{sid}/deltas  content-type: application/json; returns {acked_seq}
- WS frame types:
  "delta": <envelope>
  "ack": {session_id, acked_seq}
  "reconcile": {session_id, reconcile_ops: [<envelope>]}
  "resume_request": {session_id, from_seq}

Edge cases / open questions:
- Large payloads: if payload > 64KB, should we switch to chunked payloads or reference-by-upload (upload to pre-signed URL and include reference in payload)?
- Security: client-signed deltas? Right now rely on transport-level TLS + session tokens. Consider HMAC for offline validation in private deployments.
- Partial ordering: should we permit vector clocks for multi-client heavy concurrency? That increases complexity; postpone unless user-visible anomalies show up.
- Garbage collection: server must keep recent delta journal for gap repair; retention policy based on session activity and dedicated vs hosted customers.

Perf notes and microbench plan:
- Measure median delta size for chat product (goal: 400 bytes median). If median << 1KB, batching helps (pack multiple deltas per frame).
- Benchmarks: throughput for 1k concurrent sessions sending 1-2 deltas/sec, expected CPU cost per delta parse+apply.
- Memory: keep journal in memory for low-latency acking for hot sessions; spill to fast KV (Redis/rocks) for warm sessions.

Implementation sketch (server-side components):
- Delta ingress service: verifies session token, appends to journal, applies to working state, emits ack.
- Journal store: append-only per-session ring buffer + durable tail to storage.
- Reconciler: runs against incoming out-of-order deltas, emits reconcile ops to subscribers.

Rolling out incrementally:
1) Opt-in flag for a small set of customers (dedicated).
2) Server implements simple append/kv_set/delete ops + WS API.
3) Run shadow-mode for hosted API: accept deltas but also persist full snapshots to validate correctness.
4) Expose metrics: delta_size_hist, ack_lag_ms, gap_rate, reconcile_rate.

TODOs / next steps (short):
- [ ] prototype WS frame proto and server ingress endpoint (Diego)
- [ ] instrument delta metrics and add dashboards (Priya)
- [ ] define retention policy for journal for hosted vs dedicated (product ops)
- [ ] write compatibility guide for client SDKs (node, iOS) — define resume handshake
- [ ] evaluate chunked payload option for >64KB op payloads

Notes-to-self / rough sketches:
- Consider exposing a small op compression layer: prefix-diff for text append ops (LZW-like) + base64 payload to keep envelope JSON-friendly.
- Could piggyback token-usage hints (token_est) in payload to let server choose fast-path encoded model variants.

References and inspiration:
- existing conversation-handoff patch spec we used earlier (took some ideas)
- CRDT primer (for future)
- Dropbox rsync-ish delta chunking notes

Unresolved decisions (explicit):
- binary vs JSON envelope (JSON preferred initially for debug/observability)
- strictly monotonic delta_seq vs hybrid parent pointers (keep both for now)
- whether server should assign final reorder sequence (it should, to have canonical ordering)

End of notebook — many loose ends. This is intended to be a personal design scratchpad before carving into a proper ADR and a small prototype.
